title: Winning the Princess Theater amateur contest; mother hears him
summary: His first public win was an amateur contest at Beardstown's Princess Theater with pianist Leo Boylen; his mother and sister later heard him with the troupe in Lincoln.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh. Ah did -- where did your mother first hear you perform?
I don't know. I think -- I don't remember I think --

-- oh, I know what. I know. That last year I was in school, they was playing in the Princess Theater in Beardstown -- they had amateur contest. In the theater and there was a wonderful pianist in the pit by the name of Leo Boylen, who was a -- really a great -- he'd been with bands around territory bands --
-- and he played the silent pictures, he had all the gear, with the drums and everything, and he was a gas, I used to love to hear him play comedies and chases and things --
and so he played for me and I won, and

that's the first time she heard me play, I don't remember what I played right at the moment, I only had about four or five things I could play at that time, that I knew. I kept trying to play better all the time --
That's the first time and I won first prize, I remember that.
What did you-- was there anything involved with the first prize, that you --
But I mean when you -- when you went professionally. When this -- when this Jack Tiboo, is that his name?

I think she came someplace during the summer. I think that my mother and sister came, I think it was Lincoln, Illinois, that's how I happen to remember that town, I think they came to Lincoln and heard us.
Yeah, they thought it was like fun.
They looked at it that was, as fun. And --
